title: Ezra hears echoes of past and future

legs.note: Past: Qui-Gon, Anakin, Yoda and the Mortis Father and Daughter; individual lines are not dated.
Present: Kanan Jarrus, plus Jyn Erso and Chirrut Îmwe, all living in Ezra's own year.
Future: Kylo Ren, Rey, Finn, Poe Dameron, Maz Kanata and Leia, all sequel-era speakers.

summary: Drawn through the Lothal temple's painted gateway, Ezra crosses a starry void threaded with walkways and doors. Voices spill in from every age: Jedi from the Republic's last years, rebels of his own moment, heroes of battles decades away. It is the first sign the realm touches all times.
note: The voices are archival film and series audio; eras are assigned by speaker, not by scene.

title: Ezra pulls Ahsoka out of Malachor

legs.note: Through a doorway Ezra reaches the Malachor duel and hauls Ahsoka clear as Vader drops into the pit.
Ahsoka steps back through her own doorway into the Sith temple, alive, and walks into its depths.
Keeping her promise to find Ezra, she reappears on Lothal after the Empire's fall.

summary: Following the convor Morai, Ezra finds a door opening onto Ahsoka's fight with Darth Vader two years earlier and drags her out before the fatal blow. After they escape Palpatine she goes back to that instant alive, which is how she can resurface years later.
note: Twilight of the Apprentice shows the original duel; the Rebels epilogue is dated 9 ABY.

title: Ezra watches Kanan's sacrifice through a doorway

legs.note: A doorway shows Kanan holding back the fuel-depot fireball; Ezra decides not to pull him out.

summary: Having saved Ahsoka, Ezra wants to rescue his own master and finds the moment Kanan shields the rebels from the burning depot. Ahsoka warns that changing it would doom everyone Kanan saved. Ezra lets the moment stand and understands it as Kanan's last lesson.
note: frac values only order Kanan's death (Jedi Night) before Ezra's visit within 1 BBY.

title: Palpatine breaks into the realm between worlds

legs.note: From a ritual chamber on Coruscant, Sidious looks through Kanan's doorway and sends fire after them.

summary: Working Sith sorcery far away on Coruscant, the Emperor forces an opening into the realm and tries to seize both Force users with blue flame. Ahsoka slashes it apart, the pair split for their own doors, and Ezra seals the Lothal gateway by bringing the temple down.

title: The Emperor tempts Ezra with his parents

legs.note: A temple fragment rebuilt aboard the Chimaera opens on Mira and Ephraim calling their son home.

summary: Aboard the Chimaera, a hologram of Palpatine shows Ezra a rebuilt piece of the Lothal temple and a gateway where his parents wait, promising he can undo the past. Ezra, who felt them die, tells them goodbye and tears the structure down.
note: The gateway's destination is never dated; placing it before the parents' arrest is an inference.

title: Anakin's final lesson for Ahsoka

legs.note: Dead since Endor, Anakin's spirit meets Ahsoka in the realm and demands she fight him.
She relives the Battle of Teth, an early mission, beside her younger master.
A field station on Ryloth, where she counts the clones lost under her orders.
Mandalore's siege, a battle Anakin never saw because they had already parted.
On Seatos, Jacen Syndulla, then Hera, hear the lightsaber duel ringing up from the water.

summary: Beaten by Baylan Skoll and sunk off Seatos, Ahsoka wakes in the realm between worlds facing Anakin's spirit. He duels her through scenes of her war until she lets his red blade fall into the dark and chooses to live; then the water carries her home.
note: Ryloth has no year in its own article; the episode dates its flashbacks to 22–19 BBY.

title: The Son shows Anakin his future

legs.note: Jedi dying and a clash with Darth Sidious: the Order's end.
Betrayal on Mustafar, the turn that seals his life as Vader.
Alderaan blown apart by the Empire's first battle station.

summary: Deep in the planet's dark-side well, the Son spreads Anakin's future before him: slain Jedi, a fight with Sidious, betrayal on Mustafar, a world blown apart. Horrified, Anakin sides with the Son to change it, until the Father wipes the memory and the future stands.
note: Alderaan's destruction is dated 1 BBY by the updated Galactic Atlas.

title: Ahsoka's older self warns her away

legs.note: Her adult self says staying Anakin's student may cost her a future; she leaves the Jedi in 19 BBY.

summary: Sheltering on Mortis, Ahsoka is visited by a grown version of herself who says Anakin's darkness will corrupt her and urges her to leave him. Ahsoka defends her master. She does later leave the Order, and outlives his fall.
note: No source ties the warning to a date; linking it to her departure in The Wrong Jedi is interpretive.

title: Qui-Gon's likeness appears on Mortis

legs.note: Twelve years after Naboo, Qui-Gon warns Obi-Wan the planet may corrupt an unbalanced Anakin.
Later he sends Anakin to confront his demons in the planet's dark-side well.

summary: Mortis magnifies the Force enough for Qui-Gon to stand before Obi-Wan and, later, Anakin. He says the realm will test whether Anakin can find balance. Back home Obi-Wan calls him an illusion drawn from their memories; Anakin is less sure.
conflict: Wookieepedia's Qui-Gon article says it truly was him; the Force spirit article calls it a vision wrongly taken for a real manifestation; Obi-Wan tells the Council it was an illusion (Voices).

title: Shmi's apparition confronts Anakin's guilt

legs.note: Two years after Shmi's death on Tatooine, a figure of his mother comes to Anakin's room.

summary: In the Father's monastery a figure of Shmi visits Anakin at night. He pours out his guilt over the Tusken killings and his hidden marriage; she tells him that guilt is tearing him in two, then twists into something monstrous and is gone.
note: Whether this is Shmi or a Mortis illusion is left open.

title: The Father foretells balance for the galaxy

legs.note: Dying, the Father says Anakin balanced Mortis and will one day balance the whole galaxy.

summary: Having turned the dagger on himself to drain the Son's borrowed power, the Father names Anakin the Chosen One: he restored balance on Mortis and will someday bring the whole galaxy into balance too; he must beware his own heart. Both halves come true.
note: The episode gives no date; Endor as the fulfilment follows the Chosen One article.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: The Daughter gives Ahsoka her life

legs.note: Killed by the Son, Ahsoka revives as the dying Daughter channels her last strength into her.
Morai, a convor tied to the Daughter, guides Ezra to the door where Ahsoka is about to fall.
Morai still watches over Ahsoka on Peridea, a galaxy away.

summary: Drained by the Son, Ahsoka lies dead until the stabbed Daughter, using Anakin as a conduit, pours what life she has left into her. Ahsoka wakes remembering nothing. The convor Morai, bound to the Daughter, keeps turning up at her side for decades.
note: The Morai–Daughter link is speculation in-universe (Hydan), recorded as belief by Wookieepedia.
sources: Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord

title: Anakin dreams of his mother's pain

legs.note: The nightmares show Shmi in agony; he finds her dying, a Tusken captive.

record: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones
summary: Guarding Padmé, Anakin keeps dreaming of his mother suffering. He leaves his post for Tatooine, learns Tusken Raiders seized her a month before, and reaches her just as her life ebbs away; the grief drives the slaughter that follows.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

title: Anakin foresees Padmé dying in childbirth

legs.note: The dream comes true on Polis Massa after the twins are born, brought on by his own choices.

record: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
summary: Anakin dreams that Padmé dies giving birth and swears to stop it at any cost. That fear carries him to Palpatine and darkness; on Mustafar he chokes her, and she dies on Polis Massa after the twins arrive. Fighting the vision fulfils it.
note: frac values give relative order only.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith

title: Ahsoka dreams of Padmé's assassin

legs.note: Dreams of Aurra Sing lead Ahsoka to a refugee summit on Alderaan, where Sing strikes.

summary: Put on rest, Ahsoka keeps dreaming that the mercenary Aurra Sing is stalking someone close to her, and works out that the target is Padmé. She joins the senator's trip to Alderaan; the attack comes as foreseen, and Ahsoka keeps her alive.
note: The attempt happens and Padmé is wounded, but the killing is prevented.

title: Sifo-Dyas foresees a galactic war

legs.note: His warning is dismissed; the war begins at Geonosis a decade later, fought by his clones.

summary: Before Naboo was invaded, Sifo-Dyas sensed a vast war ahead and pressed for a Republic army. The Council judged him extreme and removed him, yet he secretly ordered clones from Kamino. The war he saw began at Geonosis, fought by that army.
note: The vision is only dated 'before the Invasion of Naboo'; he died in 32 BBY.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

title: Pong Krell foresees the Republic's fall

legs.note: Krell's vision of the Order destroyed and an Empire rising comes true within a year.

summary: Exposed as a traitor on Umbara, Krell tells Rex he has seen the Jedi exterminated and the Republic torn apart from within and remade as an Empire; he sabotaged his own troops hoping to serve the coming order. The clones execute him, but his vision holds.
note: The vision is described, not shown.

title: Maul foresees Anakin as Sidious's apprentice

legs.note: Days later Anakin kneels to Sidious, as Maul warned during the siege.

summary: Near the war's end Maul has seen that Sidious means to make Anakin his new apprentice. He lays a trap on Mandalore to kill Anakin and Kenobi before it can happen, and tells Ahsoka what is coming; she cannot act on it in time.

title: Yoda glimpses the Jedi's destruction on Dagobah

legs.note: Clones turn on Jedi and Sidious cuts down Jedi Masters, as happens at the war's end.

summary: Sent by Qui-Gon's voice into a cave on Dagobah, Yoda is overwhelmed by images of clones fighting Jedi and a Sith Lord killing a group of Masters. He stumbles out shaken, sure the Sith plan is close but unable to say when.
note: The same cave, later called the Cave of Evil, tests Luke in 3 ABY.

title: Yoda hears his own last words

legs.note: He hears 'There is another Skywalker', which he will say to Luke while dying on Dagobah.

summary: After passing the Priestesses' last trial, Yoda briefly sees ahead and hears himself speak of another Skywalker, the words he will give Luke twenty-three years later in his final moments on Dagobah.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: Bane's spectre and Sidious's illusion test Yoda

to.yText: a millennium before the Empire (c. 1019 BBY)

legs.note: Darth Bane's apparition, dead about a millennium, recounts devising the Rule of Two.
Sidious and Dooku project a false battle where Yoda can end the Sith by letting Anakin fall.

summary: On Moraband, cradle of the Sith, Yoda meets the apparition of Darth Bane, then a false present conjured by Sidious in which he can destroy the Sith only by letting Anakin die. Yoda gives himself up to save Anakin, the illusion collapses, and the trial is passed.
note: Bane's death is dated only as a millennium before the Empire, allegedly on Ambria.

title: Luke meets himself behind Vader's mask

legs.note: The warning plays out aboard Palpatine's new battle station, where Luke's rage nearly makes him his father.

record: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
summary: Sent into a dark cave on Dagobah, Luke meets a phantom Darth Vader, strikes its head off and sees his own face inside the cracked helmet. The image warns of the darkness in him, which surfaces the next year as he hacks off Vader's hand in fury.
note: Tying the vision to Luke's near-fall at Endor is interpretive; the film does not say so.
sources: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: Luke sees his friends suffering in Cloud City

legs.note: He sees Han and Leia suffering in a floating city, where Vader is torturing Han.

record: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
summary: Training on Dagobah, Luke glimpses Han and Leia in agony in a city among the clouds. Yoda says the future is hard to see, but Luke leaves for Bespin, walks into Vader's trap, loses his hand and learns who his father is.
sources: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

title: Rey touches the Skywalker lightsaber

legs.note: A Cloud City corridor, echoing with Luke's cry on learning Vader is his father.
Luke with R2-D2 by his burning temple; then the Knights of Ren standing among the dead.
Herself as a child on Jakku, screaming as her parents' ship leaves.
Kylo Ren stalking her through a snowy forest, as happens on Starkiller Base days later.
Obi-Wan's voice, old and young together, calls her name; Yoda's voice is heard too.

record: Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens
summary: Pulled to a box in Maz Kanata's cellar, Rey grips the lost lightsaber and is flung through scenes she cannot place: Cloud City, Luke's ruined temple, her own abandonment on Jakku, a snowy forest where Kylo Ren hunts her. Obi-Wan and Yoda speak through it.
note: The Knights of Ren scene is undated and grouped with the temple's fall (28 ABY).
sources: Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens

title: Luke glimpses the ruin Ben will bring

legs.note: The death Luke foresaw comes home when Ben kills Han on Starkiller Base.

record: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
summary: Reaching into his sleeping nephew's mind, Luke finds Snoke already there and feels the death and loss Ben will cause. For an instant he raises his saber; Ben wakes, fights back and brings the temple down, setting that very future in motion.
note: The vision is vague; Han's death is one inferred fulfilment among many.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition

title: Rey and Kylo glimpse each other's future

legs.note: Rey foresees Ben coming back from darkness; it happens a year later, not on the Supremacy.
Kylo sees Rey's parents and calls them nobodies who sold her and died on Jakku.
Kylo expects Rey to turn and stand with him; she never takes the dark path.

record: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
summary: When their hands meet across the Force-bond, both see something. Rey becomes certain Ben will refuse Snoke and turn; Kylo learns of her parents and becomes certain she will join him. Each acts on it aboard the Supremacy, and both are wrong that day.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
conflict: Episode VIII has Kylo call her parents junk traders who sold her; Episode IX makes them Palpatine's son and his partner, who left her on Jakku for her safety.

title: Ochi's dagger shows Rey her parents' deaths

legs.note: Gripping the blade on the Steadfast, Rey sees Ochi kill her parents in the Jakku system.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Aboard Kylo's Star Destroyer, Rey picks up the blade that Ochi of Bestoon once carried and sees what became of her parents: captured by the hunter after hiding her, they refuse to give her up and are killed.
note: Their deaths are dated 21 ABY, aboard the Bestoon Legacy in the Jakku system.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition

title: Rey faces a dark future self

legs.note: The Sith Rey she fights is the empress Palpatine tries to crown on Exegol; she refuses.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: In the Emperor's vault inside the Death Star wreck, Rey takes his wayfinder and meets herself hooded in black, a hinged red saberstaff in hand: a possible future. She loses that fight, but on Exegol she refuses the throne that future would have given her.
note: Sources call it her possible future; the tie to the Exegol offer is interpretive.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

title: Ben Solo meets the memory of Han

legs.note: A year after Ben killed him, Han appears to his son on the wrecked battle station.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: After Leia spends her life reaching him, Ben stands on the wreckage and his father is there, calling him son. Han asks him to come home; Ben hurls his lightsaber into the waves and becomes himself again.
note: Sources call Han a memory, not a Force spirit.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition

title: Ahsoka's vision of Anakin turns into Vader

legs.note: The vision confirms what happened when Anakin fell during the Order's destruction.

summary: Meditating in the Lothal temple, Ahsoka hears Anakin ask why she left him and whether she understands what he turned into. His figure becomes Darth Vader's. She spins with a blade lit and finds nothing, but can no longer deny who Vader is.
note: Reveals a past truth rather than a future.

title: A temple guard's vision knights Kanan

legs.note: The Sentinel has the Grand Inquisitor's face, from the years he guarded the Jedi Temple.
The Sentinel warns Ezra may fall; Ezra reaches for dark power on Malachor that year.

summary: Kanan duels a masked Temple Guard called the Sentinel, who says he cannot keep Ezra safe from darkness. When Kanan accepts that, the guard knights him and unmasks, revealing the Grand Inquisitor's face, the enemy Kanan killed, from the days before the Purge.
note: The Grand Inquisitor died in 4 BBY; tying the warning to Malachor is interpretive.

title: Yoda shows Ezra the Jedi at war

legs.note: Clones massing and Jedi in battle: Yoda's lesson on how fear drew the Order into war.
Yoda's last word, Malachor, sends the Jedi to the Sith world.

summary: Speaking to Ezra from afar inside the Lothal temple, Yoda shows him clone armies and fighting Jedi and explains that fear led the Order into the war that undid it. Pressed for a way to beat Vader, he reluctantly names Malachor.

title: Fused holocrons point Maul to Tatooine

legs.note: The joined Jedi and Sith holocrons show twin suns; Maul realizes Kenobi is alive.
A Nightsister spell completes the vision: a desert world under two suns.

summary: Maul makes Ezra fuse his Jedi holocron with the Sith one, and the merged light shows each what he wants. Ezra pulls away, but Maul sees enough to know Kenobi lives. A Nightsister ritual finishes the picture, and Maul goes to Tatooine to die at Kenobi's hand.
note: The holocron meeting takes place at a Mandalorian asteroid outpost, so no planet is given.

title: Ezra hears his parents in an old keycard

legs.note: A keycard in his old tower replays his parents with Tseebo, planning to resist the Empire.

summary: On the Empire's anniversary, Ezra handles an old keycard and hears his mother and father talking with their friend Tseebo about resisting Imperial rule, years before they were taken. The echo tells him where Tseebo is hiding.
note: Untrained psychometry; the parents were taken by 12 BBY, so the echo predates that.

title: Ezra's visions lead him to his parents' fate

legs.note: A dream of his imprisoned parents, a pale Loth-cat and a battle on Garel starts the search.
After learning they died freeing prisoners, Ezra sees his parents once more; they are proud.

summary: A dream shows Ezra his imprisoned parents, a pale Loth-cat and a battle on Garel. Following it to Lothal he finds Ryder Azadi, who says the Bridgers died so other prisoners could escape. That night his mother and father visit him in a vision, proud of their son.
note: The second vision is of the dead, but sources treat it as a vision rather than a Force spirit.

title: Grogu remembers the Jedi Temple's last night

legs.note: Ahsoka reads his mind: raised in the Temple, hidden after the Purge, his memories full of fear.
Luke helps him recall clones gunning down the Jedi who stood in front of him.
The Armorer's forge brings back Kelleran Beq carrying him to safety.

summary: Three times Grogu's past surfaces: Ahsoka learns his name and history through a mind touch, Luke draws out images of clones storming the Temple, and a pounding forge brings back the Jedi who died shielding him and the Master who spirited him away.
note: Legs follow release order: Mandalorian Chapter 13, then Boba Fett's Chapter 6, then Mandalorian Chapter 20.
sources: Chapter 6: From the Desert Comes a Stranger

title: Cal's echoes of the Purge and Trilla's fall

legs.note: A flashback returns Cal to Order 66, when Master Jaro Tapal died shielding him.
Holding Trilla's lightsaber, Cal sees her tortured until she becomes the Second Sister.
At the vault he sees the younglings he might gather being hunted; he later destroys the holocron.

summary: Cal can read the past in objects. On Dathomir he relives the day clones killed his master and faces Tapal's spirit underground; at the Bogano vault, Trilla's saber shows how torture remade her, and another vision shows what gathering the listed children would cost.
note: Tapal died aboard the Albedo Brave in the Bracca system. 'No' refers to the averted future vision.

title: Cal glimpses the High Republic on Koboh

legs.note: Touching Dagan's bacta tank, Cal sees the Nihil attack on Tanalorr and Dagan's past.
On the Shattered Moon he sees Santari Khri maim Dagan and seal him in bacta.

summary: Psychometry on Koboh pulls Cal two centuries back: Santari Khri's droid, Dagan Gera's discovery of Tanalorr, the Nihil raid on it, and at last Santari cutting down her obsessed friend and sealing him in bacta, where Cal has just found him still alive.
conflict: The Attack on Tanalorr is dated 232 BBY, yet Dagan Gera's article counts 224 years of stasis before 9 BBY (233 BBY), although he was sealed away after the attack.

title: Vader walks Momin's portal through his life

legs.note: His pregnant mother, and Sidious hinted as the hand behind his conception.
Doorways onto his podracing days and first moments with Padmé and Obi-Wan.
A glimpse ahead to his duel with Ahsoka on Malachor.
Cutting down phantom Jedi, he hears his grandson's voice: let the past die.

summary: After killing Darth Momin, Vader walks through the Sith's dark side gateway hoping to bring Padmé back. He drifts past scenes of his life and ahead to Malachor, slays phantom Jedi as Kylo Ren's words sound, loses Padmé again, and a vision of Luke casts him out.
note: Timelines places the issue in 12 BBY; sources call it a dark side portal, not the World Between Worlds.

title: Kylo Ren's test in Dagobah's dark cave

legs.note: Sparing his parents' phantoms foreshadows Kylo turning on Snoke aboard the Supremacy.

summary: Snoke brings Kylo to the cave on Dagobah where Luke once met his own face. Kylo kills a vision of Luke but cannot strike down the phantoms of Han and Leia, then hides that by wrecking the cave; the concealed mercy anticipates the day he kills Snoke.
note: The comic is dated only between c. 28 and 34 ABY; 31 is a placeholder midpoint.
sources: Age of Resistance - Supreme Leader Snoke 1

title: Obi-Wan's life flashes by as he dies

legs.note: Qui-Gon dying after the duel with Maul, and the funeral pyre that followed.
Newborn Luke in his arms as Padmé breathes her last.
Qui-Gon's voice wakes him to defend three-year-old Luke from raiders at the Lars farm.

summary: As Vader's blade falls on the Death Star, Obi-Wan's mind races through his life: Qui-Gon's death, Luke's birth, early years watching the boy, a bandit raid he was warned of. Then his old master tells him to let his life go, and he passes into the Force.
sources: From a Certain Point of View
conflict: Time of Death has Qui-Gon's voice guide Obi-Wan in 16 BBY; the Kenobi series shows no contact with Qui-Gon before 9 BBY. Author Cavan Scott (2026) was unsure whether it had been retconned.

title: Karr Nuq Sin's objects show the Jedi past

legs.note: Tion Medon's staff shows Obi-Wan's first meeting with the port master during the war.
Inside the Millennium Falcon he sees Obi-Wan's first lightsaber lesson for Luke.

summary: A teenager on Merokia, Karr blacks out whenever he touches certain objects, until he realizes he is seeing their history. A staff from Utapau, the Millennium Falcon's hold and an Inquisitor's broken saber show him Jedi he thought were legends, and one vision seems to show himself.

title: Luke's visions of a hidden Sith world

legs.note: Luke senses a dark world and a growing secret; Palpatine's hidden fleet rises there in 35 ABY.

summary: Long before the Emperor's return is known, Luke is troubled by visions of a dead world heavy with dark power. A possessed archaeologist's memories and a seeing stone on Tython carry him there in spirit, where Sith wraiths nearly overwhelm him.
note: Timelines places the novel in 21 ABY; linking it to 35 ABY is interpretive.

title: Maul faces phantoms in a Sith castle

legs.note: A phantom Qui-Gon, whom Maul killed, offers him freedom from the past; Maul attacks.
A phantom Grievous mocks him over the killing of Mother Talzin.
A phantom Savage Opress calls Maul's drive weakness, not vengeance.

summary: Hunting for power after the Republic's fall, Maul enters a Sith castle that raises figures from his past: his brother Savage, the cyborg who killed his mother, and Qui-Gon offering release from hatred. He attacks each, and leaves with nothing gained.
note: The story is dated only between 19 and 5 BBY; 12 BBY is a placeholder midpoint.

title: Eno Cordova foresees the Jedi Order's fall

legs.note: The Council ignores him; Order 66 proves him right.

summary: Exploring a Zeffo temple, Cordova foresees the Jedi Order's end and hurries to warn the Council, which dismisses him. Only the archivist Jocasta Nu believes him, copying for him the holocron that names Force-sensitive children, which he hides on Bogano.
note: The vision's year is not given beyond predating the Purge.

title: The Chosen One will bring balance

legs.note: Qui-Gon names Anakin the Chosen One; Anakin destroys Sidious above Endor's moon.
Obi-Wan cries that the Chosen One failed; Endor shows the prophecy delayed, not broken.
Anakin's voice urges Rey to restore balance, just as he had.

record: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace
summary: An ancient Jedi prophecy, kept on a holocron, speaks of one born of the Force and destined to end the Sith. Qui-Gon finds Anakin on Tatooine and believes it. Anakin becomes a Sith instead, until at Endor he throws Sidious down a shaft to protect Luke.
note: The prophecy's utterance is undated, so legs start at its recorded invocations.
sources: Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace
Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
conflict: Most sources credit Anakin at Endor, but Sidious returns in 35 ABY; art director Rick Carter credits Rey, Kenobi believes it is Luke (Twin Suns), and Lucas once suggested Leia.

title: The Force Priestesses foretell Yoda's destiny

legs.note: They accept Yoda because he will train someone vital to the galaxy: Luke.
They promise Qui-Gon will teach him to endure after death; he does so when he dies.

summary: On the world where midi-chlorians arise, five masked Priestesses take Yoda on because he will one day teach someone crucial to the galaxy. After his final trial they add that Qui-Gon will teach him to live on after death. Both come to pass on Dagobah.
sources: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: The Bendu foresees Thrawn's cold embrace

legs.note: The 'many arms' are purrgil that seize the Chimaera above Lothal and carry Thrawn away.

summary: Wounded after the fight on Atollon, the Bendu tells Thrawn he can see his defeat: many arms closing around him in an icy hold. Then he vanishes, laughing. A year later purrgil called by Ezra coil around the Chimaera and drag it into hyperspace.

title: Dying Maul foretells the Sith's end

legs.note: Maul trusts the Chosen One Kenobi guards will avenge them; Sidious dies at Endor.

summary: Struck down by Obi-Wan in a single exchange, Maul asks if the old Jedi is protecting the Chosen One. Told yes, he says with his last breath that he will avenge them both. Six years later Luke's refusal to kill leads Anakin to destroy Sidious.
note: Maul means Luke; that the vengeance comes through Anakin and Luke together is interpretive.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: Talzin and the Frangawl prophecy

legs.note: The foretold vanishing of the Masters and queen is staged by the cult; Talzin's ritual is stopped.
The promised era of darkness arrives anyway when the Republic becomes the Empire.

summary: Bardotta's queen warns that the vanishing of the Dagoyan Masters fulfils an old prophecy: lose the queen and darkness will spread through the galaxy. The prophecy came from the Frangawl Cult, who seize her so Mother Talzin can take her life force; Windu and Binks stop it.
note: Reading the 'era of darkness' as the Empire is an inference, not stated in the episodes.

title: The Sith Eternal's prophesied dyad

legs.note: Kylo first feels the bond probing Rey on Takodana; Sidious names the dyad on Exegol.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Sith Eternal lore foretold a Force dyad: two beings bound as one, unseen for generations. The bond Rey and Ben have felt since their first meeting proves to be it. Sidious drinks their shared life to restore himself, and their union then helps end him.
note: The prophecy's origin in Sith Eternal lore is undated; legs start at the bond's first sign.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens
Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

title: A living mythosaur heralds a new Mandalore

legs.note: The Armorer reads Bo-Katan's sighting as the promised sign; Mandalore is retaken that year.

summary: Old Mandalorian songs tell of the mythosaur rising to announce a new era. Diving after Din Djarin in the mines' sacred pool, Bo-Katan sees one alive. The Armorer takes it as the sign that Bo-Katan should unite their people, and the reconquest of Mandalore follows.
note: The songs are undated; 'partly' because a new age begins, but is not completed, on screen.

title: Qui-Gon's voice cries out to Anakin

legs.note: During the Tusken massacre Qui-Gon begs Anakin to stop; Yoda hears the cry on Coruscant.

record: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones
summary: As Anakin slaughters the Tusken camp, Qui-Gon, ten years dead, calls his name and begs him to stop. Meditating on Coruscant, Yoda hears the cry and feels Anakin's pain without grasping it; Anakin tells himself he imagined it.
note: Later canon identifies the voice as Qui-Gon's.
sources: Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones

title: Qui-Gon's voice guides Yoda's last quest

legs.note: In the Temple, Qui-Gon lifts Yoda and nearby objects to prove he is there; Anakin hears him too.
On Dagobah he shows himself as a swarm of lights and sends Yoda to the Priestesses.

summary: Late in the war Yoda hears Qui-Gon say he now belongs to the Living Force. The Council fears a Sith trick, but Yoda slips away to Dagobah, where Qui-Gon, still unable to take form, starts him toward keeping his identity after death.

title: Qui-Gon finally appears to Obi-Wan

legs.note: A voice warns Obi-Wan that three-year-old Luke is in danger from raiders.
After facing Vader, Obi-Wan sees Qui-Gon near Beggar's Canyon, who says he was always there.
As Luke races home, Qui-Gon appears nearly solid and hints they will soon be together.

summary: For a decade on Tatooine Obi-Wan calls to his old master without an answer he can trust. Only after he confronts Vader and accepts Anakin's fall does Qui-Gon stand before him in the desert. Tie-in stories add an earlier warning and a last visit before the Death Star.
sources: From a Certain Point of View
conflict: Time of Death has Qui-Gon speak to Obi-Wan in 16 BBY; the Kenobi series shows him unreachable until 9 BBY. Author Cavan Scott (2026) was unsure whether it had been retconned.

title: Obi-Wan's voice guides Luke at Yavin

legs.note: Just after dying, Obi-Wan tells Luke to run for the Falcon.
In the trench run he tells Luke to trust the Force; Luke switches off his targeting computer.

record: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
summary: Struck down by Vader, Obi-Wan vanishes, and at once his voice tells Luke to run. Over Yavin it speaks again, urging Luke to lean on the Force; he shuts off his targeting computer and destroys the Death Star.
note: The updated Galactic Atlas puts this film's pre-battle events in 1 BBY, placing the battle itself at year 0.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

title: Obi-Wan's spirit sends Luke to Yoda

legs.note: Freezing in the snow, Luke sees Obi-Wan and is told to go find Yoda on Dagobah.
Obi-Wan appears beside Yoda to warn Luke not to abandon his training.

record: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back
summary: Years after his death, Obi-Wan's shimmering figure finds Luke dying of cold on Hoth and sends him to Dagobah to learn from Yoda. Later, as a spirit beside Yoda, he pleads with Luke not to rush to Bespin; Luke goes anyway.
sources: Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back

title: Obi-Wan's spirit tells Luke of his sister

legs.note: After Yoda's death, Obi-Wan explains Anakin's fall and confirms Leia is Luke's twin.

record: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
summary: Moments after Yoda dies and vanishes, Obi-Wan appears on Dagobah to face Luke's anger: Vader really is his father, and Obi-Wan's earlier words were only half the truth. He adds that Luke's twin sister is Leia, and that Luke must confront Vader again.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: Obi-Wan, Yoda and Anakin appear at Endor

legs.note: Obi-Wan, dead for five years.
Yoda, dead since shortly before the battle.
Anakin, redeemed and dead only hours, kept whole by his old masters' teaching.

record: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi
summary: As the rebels celebrate on the forest moon, Luke looks up to see three shining figures watching him: Obi-Wan, Yoda and, restored to his younger self, Anakin Skywalker, redeemed, who perished on the battle station that day.
note: Canon says Obi-Wan and Yoda preserved Anakin's identity, since he never learned the skill.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi

title: Yoda's spirit visits Luke on Ahch-To

legs.note: Thirty years dead, Yoda calls lightning down on the old Jedi tree and teaches Luke once more.

record: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
summary: As Luke moves to burn the ancient Jedi tree, Yoda appears, cackling, and does it for him with a lightning strike. He reminds his old pupil that failing is how masters learn and that Rey needs him, freeing Luke to face Kylo Ren one last time.
note: The sacred texts were already safe aboard the Millennium Falcon.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi

title: Luke's spirit ends Rey's exile

legs.note: One year after dying, Luke catches his father's lightsaber and raises his sunken fighter.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Horrified to learn she is Palpatine's granddaughter, Rey hides on Ahch-To and tosses Anakin's lightsaber into a fire. Luke's spirit catches it, admits he was wrong to hide, gives her Leia's saber, and hauls his old fighter up from the depths so she can reach Exegol.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

title: Generations of Jedi speak to Rey

legs.note: Qui-Gon: every past Jedi lives on inside her.
Mace Windu, Aayla Secura, Adi Gallia and Luminara Unduli, all dead by the Purge.
Obi-Wan, heard in both his older and younger voice.
Kanan Jarrus tells her a Jedi's strength lies in the heart.
Anakin asks her to bring balance back, as he once had; Yoda says she was never alone.
Luke's voice closes the chorus with a blessing.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Drained and beaten beneath Palpatine's citadel, Rey asks the Jedi to be with her. Voices from generations she knows only by name answer: Qui-Gon, Mace, Obi-Wan, Kanan, Ahsoka, Anakin, Yoda, Luke. Lifted by them, she stands and turns Palpatine's lightning back on him.
note: Adi Gallia died in 19 BBY; Luminara Unduli between 19 and 18 BBY; both grouped at 19 BBY.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition
conflict: Ahsoka Tano's voice is among them, though no canon source shows her death by 35 ABY; the Force spirit article also notes some speakers, like Mace Windu, were voices rather than full spirits.

title: Luke and Leia watch Rey become a Skywalker

legs.note: Luke, dead since his standoff with Kylo at Crait.
Leia, who gave her life reaching Ben only days before.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: At the empty Lars homestead, Rey buries the twins' lightsabers in the sand. When a passing woman asks her name, she glances up and sees Luke's and Leia's spirits watching, and answers: Rey Skywalker.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker

title: Anakin's spirit watches Ahsoka on Peridea

legs.note: Stranded with Sabine after the battle, Ahsoka is watched over by her master's spirit.

record: Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord
summary: Left behind on Peridea after Thrawn escapes and Ezra slips home, Ahsoka and Sabine gaze at an alien sky. Unseen by them, Anakin's spirit stands close by, keeping watch over his old apprentice in another galaxy.
sources: Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord

title: Kanan's will speaks through the wolf Dume

legs.note: In a dream, the white wolf bearing Kanan's birth name hands Ezra the temple's key stone.
Collapsing after the temple is sealed, Ezra hears Kanan's voice bless him one last time.

summary: After Kanan dies saving his friends, a huge white Loth-wolf calling itself Dume, Kanan's birth name, finds Ezra and points him toward the temple to set the past right and save the future. Ahsoka later explains the wolf carries Kanan's will.
note: Not a classic Force spirit: sources call Dume a manifestation of Kanan's will.

title: Anakin's spirit rescues Luke from Exegol

legs.note: Anakin scatters Sith wraiths with a lightsaber and sends Luke's spirit back to Tython.

summary: Meditating on a seeing stone on Tython, Luke finds himself on Exegol, where nine wraiths close in and his blade passes through them. His father appears with a lightsaber, drives them off and returns Luke to Tython, spending nearly all his strength to do it.
note: The novel is dated 21 ABY by Star Wars: Timelines.

title: Nightsister spirits claim a debt on Dathomir

legs.note: Spirits of Nightsisters, whose clan was massacred in the war, possess Kanan and Sabine.

summary: Maul's borrowed Nightsister spell works, but the dead witches who fed it want flesh as payment. Two spirits rise from the altar and take over Kanan and Sabine. Ezra offers himself instead, then smashes the altar; the witches vanish screaming.
note: Dark-side spirits, not Force spirits; the Nightsister massacre is dated 20 BBY (Massacre).

title: Kenobi's warning to surviving Jedi

legs.note: Caleb Dume, bound for Coruscant through hyperspace, receives the warning and turns away.
Cere Junda saved the broadcast to a holocron; it plays during Cal Kestis's mission.
Ezra opens Kanan's holocron and hears the message; Kanan later plays it in full.
The holocron replays the warning in the night, starting Ezra's search for Kenobi.

record: Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion
summary: In the fallen Temple, Obi-Wan and Yoda turn the recall beacon into a warning, and Obi-Wan records a message: the Order has fallen, stay away, trust the Force, a new hope will come. Survivors catch it that day, and holocron copies carry it to new Jedi years later.
note: Episode III shows the beacon being changed; the recorded wording is heard in Rebels.
sources: Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith
Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion

title: Leia's hidden plea reaches Obi-Wan

legs.note: Recorded into R2-D2 aboard the Tantive IV, it reaches Kenobi through Luke days later.

record: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope
summary: As Vader's troops storm her ship, Leia records a plea into R2-D2 and sends him to Tatooine with the stolen plans. The droid shows a fragment to Luke, then the whole message to Obi-Wan, who answers the call and ends his exile.
note: Spans days, not years; included as the saga's founding message across distance.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope

title: Ezra's farewell hologram outlives his disappearance

legs.note: Chopper plays it right after the Chimaera vanishes: Ezra had to go, and hopes to come home.
Sabine is still replaying it in her tower a decade later.
Ahsoka switches it on while searching Sabine's home for clues.

summary: Before letting the purrgil carry him and Thrawn away, Ezra records a goodbye: he had to choose this path, he left fruit for Hera, and he is counting on Sabine. Years later she still watches it, alone in her Lothal tower.

title: Anakin's training holograms outlast his fall

legs.note: Ezra and Ahsoka study recordings of Anakin's saber lessons aboard Hera's ship.
Riding a purrgil between galaxies, Ahsoka spars against her master's hologram.

summary: Anakin's recorded dueling lessons survive him. Ezra studies them to fight better, and Ahsoka, who has not seen her master in years, watches them in Kanan's cabin; a decade later she still trains against the hologram in deep space.
note: The recordings are undated; in Part Seven Anakin names Grievous, Ventress and Dooku, placing them in the war.

title: The sacred Jedi texts pass to Rey

legs.note: Books from the Order's dawn, gathered by Luke in the Ahch-To tree, are taken by Rey.
Rey studies them at the Resistance base, relearning forgotten techniques.

record: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
summary: Eight books and scrolls from the Jedi Order's earliest days sit in a hollow tree on Ahch-To, collected by Luke. When Yoda's lightning burns the tree, Rey has already hidden them aboard the Falcon, and she later pores over them to recover lost skills.
note: Dated from the Rammahgon, whose original was lost over five millennia before 35 ABY; the collection may be older.
sources: Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi
Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary

title: Sifo-Dyas's final message, found twice

legs.note: A signal from his downed shuttle leads Plo Koon to Sifo-Dyas's lightsaber.
Karr Nuq Sin digs up a holoprojector holding the Jedi's last message about the clones.

summary: Shot down over a moon of Oba Diah, Sifo-Dyas left a wreck that kept signalling. Near the war's end it draws Plo Koon to his lightsaber, reopening the question of who ordered the clones; decades later a boy finds his recorded message buried in the sand.
note: The site is a moon of Oba Diah; the planet stands in as place.

title: Eno Cordova's recordings lead Cal on

legs.note: BD-1 plays Cordova's first message; later ones on Zeffo, Kashyyyk and Dathomir guide Cal.

summary: Before the Purge, Eno Cordova hid a holocron naming Force-sensitive children inside a Zeffo vault and had BD-1 record messages about his journey, a trail of tests for whoever followed. Five years into the Empire, Cal traces them one by one.
note: The recordings predate the Purge but carry no exact date; Cordova himself lived until 9 BBY.

title: Santari Khri's message waits two centuries

legs.note: Dagan watches her recording in the observatory; Cal's crew finds the full version and its route.

summary: Having sealed Dagan Gera in bacta rather than kill him, Santari Khri left a message for his waking: seek her out, or keep chasing Tanalorr. Two hundred years later he watches part of it before his last duel, and Cal's crew uses the rest to chart a route to Tanalorr.
note: Recording date follows Dagan's stasis count (224 years before 9 BBY).

title: Obi-Wan's journal left for Luke

legs.note: Luke reads Ben's account of looking after him years before, among other stories from exile.

summary: During his exile Obi-Wan kept a journal of his Tatooine years: quiet rescues, attempts to reach Qui-Gon, notes on lightsaber building. After Yavin, Luke recovers it from Ben's home, where it was left for him, and reads his guardian's stories.
note: Entries span the whole exile; the first story told is dated 9 or 8 BBY.

title: A holocron leads Luke to Elzar Mann

legs.note: A recorded Yoda in a Jedi holocron teaches Luke about visions and names Gazian.
The living planet kept Elzar Mann's mind as he was; the imprint talks with Luke.

summary: A Yoda recording in a holocron sends Luke to Gazian, a living vergence. Trapped there, he meets the preserved mind of Elzar Mann, a Jedi of the Republic's golden era, who guesses he must be long dead and tells Luke the path is hard but worth it.
note: Neither recording is dated; Elzar Mann flourished during the High Republic, c. 232 BBY onward.

title: Palpatine returns from death

legs.note: Killed at Endor, Sidious lives on in a failing clone; a galaxy-wide broadcast announces him.
Already reborn, he reaches Ochi in a spiritual encounter and orders Rey's capture.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Hurled down a reactor shaft at Endor, Sidious moves his essence into a cloned body on Exegol, kept alive by the Sith Eternal. Decades later a broadcast reveals him, and at the end he feeds on Rey and Ben's bond to make himself whole.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition
Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith
conflict: Wookieepedia articles differ on timing: one has him transfer just before his original body's destruction, another after its death. The film itself gives no mechanism.

title: Darth Momin is reborn on Mustafar

legs.note: Bodiless for a millennium in his mask, Momin uses Vader's fortress to rebuild himself, then dies again.

summary: Destroyed by his own city-killing weapon a millennium earlier, Momin lives on as a mind in his mask. Given to Vader, the mask shapes Fortress Vader into a gateway of dark power, and Momin uses it to regain a body before Vader kills him once more.
note: Star Wars: Timelines dates his first death to c. 1100–1000 BBY; 1050 is a placeholder midpoint.

title: Ventress chooses to return to life

legs.note: Laid in Dathomir's waters months after dying, she is offered a way back.
Mother Talzin, herself dead, speaks from beyond and names the price: her heart's desire.
Alive again, she resurfaces in the Empire's early years and meets the Bad Batch.

summary: Killed saving Quinlan Vos, Ventress is carried home and laid to rest in her clan's sacred pools. There, dead, she hears Mother Talzin: Vos's love is a gift, and she may go back at the cost of what she most wants. She steps back into life and a quiet existence.

title: Ben Solo gives his life to revive Rey

legs.note: Rey dies destroying Palpatine; Ben pours his own life into her, and she wakes as he fades.

record: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
summary: Climbing from the pit after Palpatine's end, Ben finds Rey lifeless. He uses the healing she once used on him, giving his own life force. She wakes, they embrace, and he dies and vanishes, the final heir of Anakin's line.
sources: Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker
